name: Möckern (Leipzig)

art.title: The Brandenburg Hussars' Charge at Möckern

summary: North of Leipzig, while Napoleon fought the Army of Bohemia at Wachau, Blücher's Army of Silesia came down the Halle road. Marmont, ordered south to join the Emperor, turned back to hold a line from Möckern on the Elster to Lindenthal, with his reserve guns massed in the centre. Yorck's Prussians attacked in the afternoon: Möckern was stormed and retaken five times, his battalions melting under the French guns, until in the evening the Brandenburg Hussars and the reserve cavalry charged through and Marmont's line broke. It cost Yorck a third of his corps, and Marmont nearly as much; to the east Langeron's Russians drove back Dombrowski's Poles.

forces.name: Compans's Division
forces.summary: Marmont's left, round Möckern itself, where the village by the Elster was taken and lost again and again through the afternoon; Compans was wounded, and the marines of his division fought house by house until the Prussian cavalry broke through.
notes: Built from A Clash of Eagles' French 1812 list, the nearest to 1813: there is no list for the army Napoleon raised after Russia, largely of conscripts and of battalions drawn from depots all over the Empire.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Möckern, from the Prussian General Staff's plans and the French archives.
Its marine regiments were sailors and naval gunners of the fleet's artillery, brought inland in 1813; they fought well, and are shown as Line, the list's Veteran upgrade would suit them.
Its battalions were down to three or four hundred men; they are shown at full size, and the list's Small upgrade would suit many of them.
The division's two foot batteries, where the list allows one, show as a historical departure.

Marmont's corps reserve artillery, which formed the great battery between Möckern and Lindenthal, is with this division: two 12-pdr, a 6-pdr and a horse battery. Its two 12-pdr batteries, where the list allows one for the division's battalions, and its horse battery with no cavalry to allow it, show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.

forces.name: Yorck's Corps
forces.summary: Yorck's corps attacked Marmont's line from the north in the early afternoon. Möckern was taken and lost five times; Hünerbein and Steinmetz were wounded and whole battalions shot away, until in the evening Yorck sent in the Brandenburg Hussars and the reserve cavalry, which broke through the French line. The corps lost nearly 8,000 men, a third of its strength, the costliest single fight of the battle.
notes: Built from Albion Triumphant's Prussian 1815 list, the nearest to 1813: its Prussian Infantry Brigade is the 1813 brigade, the size of another army's division, with line, reserve and Landwehr battalions.

After Nafziger's order of battle for Wartenburg, a fortnight before: his return of the corps the day after Möckern shows its battalions merged by the losses there, so it doesn't show the corps as it began the fight.
After Nafziger's order of battle for Wartenburg, from Mirus's history of the fight.
A Prussian brigade was the size of another army's division, so the whole corps is here. Take the brigades you want; each is a force in itself.

Battalions of different regiments that served together are grouped as a regiment, as the list takes them. Reserve battalions are the list's Musketeers; grenadier battalions are Musketeers with its Veteran upgrade.
Brigades of three regiments or more have a Subordinate Commander, named where the order of battle names the brigade's infantry commander.

Nafziger's corps return of the same day has Hünerbein's Landwehr and half his battery detached to Halle; his Wartenburg order of battle, followed here, has the IV/14th Landwehr and the whole of Battery #15 with the brigade.
The East Prussian National Cavalry, a volunteer regiment, is shown as Hussars. The 5th Silesian Landwehr Cavalry is the advance guard infantry's attached Landwehr cavalry.

Mecklenburg's two hussar regiments are shown as attached small hussars; two of them, where the list allows one in the army, show as a historical departure. Battery #3 was split between Mecklenburg and Horn, so each has half of it, Mecklenburg's from the corps artillery.
One-battalion Landwehr regiments in Mecklenburg's and Hünerbein's brigades, Horn's four regiments, and Jürgass's line and Landwehr cavalry brigades together show as historical departures.
Commanders are at Staff Rating 8, the default for historical forces.
